timeline.say: When a shoot falls apart, the fastest fix often quietly drops someone — a step-free route, an interpreter. All-Access recovers the day without trading those away, and proves the plan reached everyone.
Day fourteen of Salt and Light. Five scenes, three locations — every approved access arrangement satisfied.
Weather and scenes on one axis. The amber bars are exterior work.
A verified storm reaches the harbour at eighteen thirty. Sixty-eight kilometre winds, sea state six.
Source event to verified readiness — the whole loop — in under half a second. Nothing on this screen is a recording.
The event arrives typed, contract-validated and hash-chained, carrying the authority that says whether the system may act without a human first.
The digital twin traverses the dependency graph — a hundred and nineteen affected entities across six levels.
Distance from the centre is how far the storm had to travel. Each wedge is one kind of thing.
The purple rings are approved access arrangements. A scheduling tool would have shown the replacement location as free.
The obvious move is the boatshed. It is available. The system will not publish it.
A minimal conflict set: C-ACC-001, a step-free route to the working position — with the owner and the approved arrangement it comes from.
Not “infeasible”. Why — and whether the rule may be waived. This one may not.
Underneath it, the survey: the shed door's cill is a hundred and forty millimetres against a twenty limit. A location manager can act on that — not on 'accessibility concern'.
Three structurally different plans, each rechecked against all thirty-four constraints independently, before any was shown to anyone.
Objectives trade off. Hard constraints trade off against nothing — which is why the access row reads the same on all three.
The system approves nothing. Two named authorities sign, and each signature is bound to the plan hash and the constraints in force — single use, expiring.
Nine typed commands through the saga coordinator. Every one completed. Every acknowledgment returned.
A system that trusted that would call the day ready. This one refuses — props hasn't accepted — and there is no override.
Across a thousand disruptions, verification caught seventy-five of seventy-five incomplete executions — twelve percent of runs that would otherwise have closed early.
For the producer, not the incident but the shift: which rules removed the most options, who owns them, and where they came from — a list you can spend money against.
Every screen is a fold over one event log. Replay it into a fresh view and it reproduces live state exactly, hash chain intact.
